items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: And in the trumpet section he had Dizzy, Fats Navarro, Shorty McConnell... Tommy Potter playing bass. Well, Tommy got a case of pneumonia, so they called me out to substitute for him

ctx.x: But he could take -- he was so windy, he could take such large breaths that the rest of the saxophone section couldn't phrase with him, see, because he would hold out until he would turn red in the face, you know, to get a phrase through, and they couldn't follow him. So he couldn't keep a job because of this. He was just too good, you know. So he was so good that he quit playing music and went back to law school for a year and got his shingle, and he put it out in the Loop. He started passing. He was…

Anyway, after Earl Hines' band, then Billy Eckstine formed a band, and he got all of the stars, you know. And he had -- at one time, he had -- let's see, in the reed section he had Dexter Gordon, Budd Johnson, Little Johnny Jackson -- I can't remember who the other one was. And in the trumpet section he had Dizzy, Fats Navarro, Shorty McConnell, and someone else I can't recall. I don't have total recall on the band. And he had two trombone players. One was Chippie Outcoul and another little trombone player out of…

did know his name. John Malachi playing piano. Art Blakey at the drums. And Tommy Potter playing bass. Well, Tommy got a case of pneumonia, so they called me out to substitute for him, and I had been laying off for awhile, you know, fingers were soft and everything, callouses were soft. And boy, it was a labor job the first night. So the next night I went prepared. I soaked my hands in powdered alum and hot water, as hot as I could stand it, you know, until they were water soaked, you know, like you see when…
